panels.title: Run workflow (what the supervising workflow is doing)
Workflow phase
panels.description: The phase a workflow supervising the run reports (sip_soak_phase): bring-up, launching, running, investigating, remediating, reporting, done. An empty board in bring-up means the lab is still coming up, not that the system under test is down.

panels.title: Incident events: seen / expected
panels.description: How far through its planned incidents the supervised run is.

panels.title: Findings escalated this run
panels.description: One row per root-cause signature the supervising workflow escalated (sip_soak_finding), with its severity.

panels.title: Concurrent calls (all streams)
panels.description: Live established dialogs across long+short+abuse+peak.

panels.title: Call setup rate (created/s)
panels.description: Aggregate INVITEs/s created by all UAC streams.

panels.title: Success ratio (5m, excl. abuse+limiter)
panels.description: Resolved-call success ratio over 5m for REAL traffic (abuse excluded — the abuse stream is adversarial by design and floors at ~1 unexpected_msg/call; see the abuse-apart panel).

panels.title: Failed calls (cumulative, excl. abuse+limiter)
panels.description: Total failed calls across REAL streams (abuse excluded — counted apart in the abuse panel).

panels.title: Concurrent calls by stream
panels.description: Live dialogs per traffic role.

panels.title: Call rate by stream
panels.description: SIPp cumulative call rate (cps) per role.

panels.title: Successful vs failed (calls/s, excl. abuse+limiter)
panels.description: Per-second resolved call outcomes for REAL traffic (abuse stream excluded — counted apart below).

panels.title: Failure causes (calls/s, excl. abuse+limiter)
panels.description: Per-second failures by SIPp failure class for REAL traffic (abuse excluded — its steady ~1/s unexpected_msg is adversarial-by-design and counted apart below).

panels.title: Failure causes (cumulative) by stream
panels.description: Cumulative count per failure class AND per SIPp stream/endpoint (role + scenario), non-zero only. This attributes each 'unexpected_msg' (and every other cause) to the exact stream that saw it.

panels.title: Retransmissions / out-of-call / dead-call (per-s)
panels.description: Protocol-health signals.

panels.title: Worker / proxy restarts (SUT)
panels.description: Container restart counters — chaos kills show here.

panels.title: SUT pod CPU (cores)
panels.description: cAdvisor CPU per worker/proxy pod.

panels.title: B2BUA active calls per worker (must fall to ~0 when idle — leak detector)
panels.description: b2bua_active_calls per worker. A flat plateau after traffic stops = the call leak. With the reaper fix it tracks real concurrency and drains.

panels.title: Ghost gap = b2bua_active − sipp_current − loadgen_inflight (double-serve leak detector, ADR-0014)
panels.description: The HA leak signal: the workers' active calls against the calls the generators hold (SIPp current calls plus the loadgens' calls in flight, which are the workers' calls too). A healthy cluster keeps the gap near 0 (plus scrape skew). A gap that rises and stays risen after a worker restart is a call served twice: a takeover copy the restarted primary serves as well (self-release failed), or an eager-takeover storm (ADR-0014). The threshold line is 300. A product call with several legs (a reroute, a transfer, a media leg) can hold more than one B2BUA call per generator call, so such a load keeps a positive gap at rest: read its trend, not its level.

panels.title: Messages/sec per stream (calls created by role)
panels.description: `sipp_calls_created_total` rate split by SIPp instance (role: long / short / abuse / peak / orphan). Each stream counts its own traffic; all roles share this graph.

panels.title: Errors/sec per stream (failed calls by role)
panels.description: `sipp_failed_calls_total` rate split by SIPp instance (role). Each stream counts its own failures; all roles share this graph so you can see which endpoint is erroring.

panels.title: Unexpected messages by endpoint (role + scenario)
panels.description: `sipp_failed_total{cause="unexpected_msg"}` rate split by the SIPp instance that received it (role + scenario). This is the answer to 'which endpoint generated the unexpected message'.

panels.title: Failure causes per stream (cause + role)
panels.description: `sipp_failed_total` rate by failure class AND SIPp instance (role) — full per-endpoint error breakdown across every cause, not just unexpected_msg.

panels.title: Abuse stream — counted apart (EXCLUDED from headline)
panels.description: The adversarial abuse stream (uac-abuse-options-flood) in isolation: calls/s, failures/s and failure causes. By design it floors at ~1 unexpected_msg per call (the flood's responses don't match the scenario's recv expectations), so it is excluded from the headline success/failure panels and tracked here instead. Real baseline (short/long) carries the headline.

panels.title: Call-limiter stream — SIPp concurrent vs cap
panels.description: The dedicated limiter stream (uac-endurance-limiter-cap20, role=limiter) admitted-and-held concurrency, shown APART from the other streams. A healthy limiter pins this at the cap (20); the 486-rejected calls never enter hold so this is the clean cap signal the endurance limiter_kill/limiter_netcut events assert reconvergence on (within LIMITER_GRACE). Other calls all carry the global-stress:999999 entry so the limiter chain is stressed on every call, but only this stream is capped.

panels.title: Call-limiter — admit vs rejected (per-s)
panels.description: Limiter service throughput: admits/s (every call traverses the limiter — global-stress chain stress) vs rejected/s (the cap-20 stream biting). Reject rate should be ~0 except for the limiter stream's over-cap calls; it drops to 0 during limiter_kill/limiter_netcut (b2bua fails open) then resumes.

panels.title: Re-hydration: bootstrap outcome (passes/min)
panels.description: A rebooting primary pulls its partition back from the backup. SEEDED = a pass reached the terminal Noop (full keyset streamed). STALLED = a pass tripped the (now 2-min) idle window — the stream went silent mid-rehydration. Persistent STALLED = a peer-side stall truncating the stream, not the materialisation.

panels.title: Re-hydration: bodies imported per bootstrap pass (last_applied)
panels.description: Bodies the MOST RECENT bootstrap pass imported, per worker. After a kill, this should jump to ~the worker's held partition size. If successive STALLED passes re-pin last_applied at the SAME value, the stream is truncating (peer-side stall) — the failure class behind the long-call-on-reboot 481.

panels.title: Reclaim: calls re-materialised into the serving map
panels.description: b2bua_repl_reclaimed_total = calls the rebooted primary materialised into its LIVE serving map + re-armed timers (now puller-driven & continuous, not a one-shot 10s-bounded sweep). After a kill this should climb to ~the reclaimed worker's pre-kill long+short concurrency. A flat/short climb = incomplete rebuild (the stranding bug).

panels.title: Reactive takeover vs self-release (rate/min)
panels.description: ADR-0014 reactive-only takeover: the backup hydrates a dialog on demand when the proxy reroutes (takeover_hydrated) and self-releases the copy once the served txn terminates (self_release), or stands it down on a covering write of its returned primary (stand_down, ADR-0047 D7). Balanced rates ⇒ no double-serve buildup.

panels.title: Reverse flush refused per worker in range (must stay far below takeover_hydrated)
panels.description: ADR-0014: a backup's reverse flush for a call this primary serves live that neither the (p,b) vector nor lifecycle progress let it fold, so the primary kept its own copy. A count near takeover_hydrated means the answered body is not reaching the fold: established calls are being lost.

panels.title: Incident windows (1 while open)
panels.description: Each incident window of a run (sip_chaos_window), from its inject to its close at recovery plus the settle time. The same windows shade every dashboard as annotations.

panels.title: Incident phases in range
panels.description: Every phase an incident reached in the time range (sip_chaos_event): inject, injected, heal, healed, recovered, or failed when a step failed or overran.

panels.title: Verdict per window
panels.description: Each window's verdict when its run's verdict was written: pass, fail (impacts above the window's budget, counted in findings) or invalid (its incident failed). verdict.json holds the impacts. Filtered by the run variable.

panels.title: Run verdicts
panels.description: The verdict of each run whose verdict was written in the time range: pass, fail or invalid (an integrity problem: the run cannot charge the system under test).

panels.title: Records by stream, shape and ending (calls/s)
panels.description: The call-outcome records the generators write, one per call placed: SIPp UACs (sipp_records_total) and loadgens (loadgen_outcome_records_total), by stream, shape and ending.

panels.title: Endings other than answered, by reason (records per interval)
panels.description: Call-outcome records in the log store whose ending is not answered, by stream, shape, ending and reason (the SIP code, a Reason protocol cause, timeout, transport or protocol). Filtered by the run variable.

targets.expr: _stream:{run=~"$run"} | unpack_json from _msg fields (schema, reason, final_code) keep_original_fields | schema:="call-outcome.v1" !ending:=answered | stats by (stream, shape, ending, reason) count() calls

panels.title: Outcomes in range by stream, shape, ending, code and reason
panels.description: Every call-outcome record in the time range, counted by stream, shape, ending, final code and reason. Filtered by the run variable.

targets.expr: _stream:{run=~"$run"} | unpack_json from _msg fields (schema, reason, final_code) keep_original_fields | schema:="call-outcome.v1" | stats by (stream, shape, ending, final_code, reason) count() calls

panels.title: Calls offered and never recorded (calls/s)
panels.description: Calls a loadgen offered that left no record: refused before any datagram (not placed) or failed by the generator itself, by stream, shape and reason. Either is the generator's, never the system's.

panels.title: Record shipping to the log store (must stay at 0)
panels.description: Records not yet posted, failed posts and records lost on their way to the log store. A record lost is a record gap: the run's verdict turns invalid.

panels.title: Offered calls per stream (calls/s)
panels.description: Calls each stream placed. A load-incident stream (a spike) shows from its incident's inject to its heal, inside the incident's window.

panels.title: Calls in flight per stream
panels.description: Calls each stream holds open. A load-incident stream drains to 0 at heal, or stops at once when its incident abandons it.

panels.title: Failed calls per stream (calls/s)
panels.description: Calls each stream counted failed: SIPp's failed calls and loadgen calls classed other than ok. The verdict judges the records, against the budget of each window.

panels.title: Host under the run (pressure and swap: a stall here is the host's, not the SUT's)
Host full pressure (share of time stalled)
panels.description: Sampled by the hakit runner every second for the whole run (/proc/pressure, /proc/vmstat). A generator stall inside a stressed interval is reported as host_under_stress.

panels.title: Host swap (pages/s)
panels.description: Sampled by the hakit runner every second for the whole run (/proc/pressure, /proc/vmstat). A generator stall inside a stressed interval is reported as host_under_stress.
